message.reasoning:
I need to decide on a bid for the Marvin Gardens auction.

I have $424 and am on Atlantic Avenue. My holdings include two of three pinks and one of three reds. I still need Virginia and the orange group.

Player 3 has two of three yellows and would complete the yellow monopoly with Marvin Gardens. Player 4 owns a nearly fully built light blue set with four houses on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut. Player 1 holds dangerous dark blue properties with two to three houses. The current high bid is $300 from player 4.

The minimum next bid is $301. Player 1 has dropped out. My previous ceiling for winning was $180 to $200, but player 4's $300 bid already exceeds that. I am now weighing whether to block player 3 from completing the yellow monopoly or let player 4 win.

Winning would leave me with roughly $123, too little to buy Virginia and complete the pink set. Player 4 already blocks player 3 with his $300 bid, so I should drop out.

I will drop out. Player 3 could bid up to $596 and player 4 to $634, so I will not chase past $200. If player 3 wins at a high price, they would spend heavily but own an unimproved yellow monopoly with modest rents.

Player 3 would need roughly $450 to build one house on each yellow property. A $300 bid leaves them with about $296, but a higher price would leave only $146 and prevent immediate development. I am now weighing whether to push the auction higher to force player 3 to overpay.

A $350 bid would leave only about $74, which is catastrophic. Player 3 wants the yellow monopoly badly, so both players are unlikely to drop out immediately. The dark blue set with three houses on Boardwalk costs $1400 in rent.

I cannot afford the rent from either the dark blue or light blue monopolies. Park Place with two houses costs $500, and Boardwalk with three houses costs $1400. The light blue set with four houses each costs $450. My $424 cash is insufficient for any of these. I would need to mortgage my pink properties to survive. St. Charles Place and States Avenue mortgage for about $70 each. Indiana Avenue mortgages for roughly $110.

Mortgaging my remaining properties would raise about $440, giving total liquidity near $864. That covers the rent from the light blue and Park Place sets but still falls short of Boardwalk with three houses. Even after winning the auction, cash would drop to roughly $124, leaving only about $564 in total. I cannot afford to buy Virginia without mortgaging first. The priority remains completing the pink set.

Player 4's $300 bid already blocks player 3. I should drop out rather than chase. If I bid $301, player 4 might drop and player 3 might back down, leaving me stuck with a non-monopoly property and only about $123 cash.

Player 3 is trying to get us to burn cash for him. He bid only $150 and wants the auction to stay cheap so he can grab the yellow monopoly. Player 4 at $300 already blocks him. I will drop out and let the two fight it out.

I will drop out and tell player 4 to keep bidding. I want player 3 to overpay for the yellow monopoly so he bleeds cash. Player 4 is the biggest threat with his light blue set, so I must not help him too much.
